newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa revises 1996/97 sugar crop to 2.27 mln T.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa revises 1996/97 sugar crop to 2.27 mln T.

text.p: South Africa will produce 2.27 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 season down from the previous estimate of 2.37 million tonnes, industry officials said on Thursday.

The latest crop estimate from the South African Canegrowers' Association shows that an estimated 20.95 million tonnes of cane will be crushed in the season (April-March) which will yield an estimated 2.27 million tonnes of sugar.
"That estimate will be very close to our final production," an industry official said.
Most sugar mills had finished crushing cane for the season and most deliveries had been completed, he added.
Officials said the drop in estimated production could be attributed to bad weather conditions and production problems at some sugar mills.
But even with the crop reduced to 2.27 million tonnes, it will be the best in several years.
South Africa produced only 1.67 million tonnes in the 1995/96 season and was just emerging from five years of drought which the industry said cost it millions of rands in lost revenue.
A crop of 2.27 million tonnes would leave just under a million tonnes for export and the South African Sugar Association said last year it had sold virtually all this season's export surplus.
